title: Chat across four servers
question: Your chat app now runs on four servers. A user on server A sends a message to a friend connected to server C, and it never arrives. What is missing?
context: Each server keeps its WebSocket connections in memory and writes messages to PostgreSQL. Single-server deployments worked perfectly.

options.label: Sticky sessions so friends always land on the same server
options.why: You cannot guarantee two arbitrary users share a server, and sticky routing defeats load balancing. It papers over the real gap.

options.label: A shared Pub/Sub channel every server subscribes to
options.why: Server A publishes the message; every server receives it and delivers to recipients it holds connections for. This is the standard fan-out layer between stateful WebSocket servers.

options.label: Each server polls PostgreSQL for new messages every second
options.why: Works badly: latency of up to a second, heavy read load and no ordering guarantees. The database is the history store, not the real-time bus.

options.label: Switch the WebSocket connections to Server-Sent Events
options.why: The transport is not the problem — SSE servers would have exactly the same isolated in-memory connection tables.
